subject: Post-call: Private VPC dataflow & PII retention — FinSecure next steps

Subject: Post-call: Private VPC dataflow & PII retention — FinSecure next steps

Hi Alice / Bob — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have a shared picture.

Summary of what we covered
- Scope: private/VPC deployment for production inference (no hosted public endpoints), customer-data-only tenancy.
- PII concerns: FinSecure considers customer account numbers, SSNs, and full-card PANs as high-sensitivity PII; you want confirmation that these do not leave the VPC or get persisted to any Redwood-hosted logs.
- Retention: you asked for options to set request payload retention to zero and restrict audit/log retention to customer-managed storage.
- On-prem/air-gapped: feasible but will require an air-gapped installer + offline key exchange and an ops runbook.

What Redwood can provide (high level)
- Private deployment (VPC) with strict egress controls: default deny, only explicit endpoints allowed.
- BYOK (customer-managed KMS) for data-at-rest encryption and for disk-level keys.
- Configurable logging: request payload retention can be set to 0; structured request metadata and audit logs can be pushed to customer-managed S3 or syslog over private connectivity.
- KV cache: can be configured RAM-only or encrypted (no persistent unencrypted disk cache).
- On-prem / air-gapped packaging available — we will need a week for packaging + a short on-site/remote install plan.

Attachments: redwood-private-vpc-dataflow.pdf (dataflow + network boundary diagram), redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (SOC 2 scope summary). I’ve attached the files for your security team.

Open questions for you (so we can scope the MAP)
1) Data residency: is primary residency required in US-only or do you have EU customer datasets that must remain in EU regions?
2) Can you share a network diagram (we can overlay required peering/IPs)?
3) Do you require zero payload retention by default across all environments or only in production?

Proposed next steps
- Schedule technical deep-dive (Vivek + Marcus + Monica) to walk through dataflow and network boundary: propose Wed Mar 17, 10:00–11:00 PT.
- Marcus to produce an initial private-deployment cost estimate and license proposal (due Fri Mar 19).
- Monica to send blank security questionnaire for your security team to fill out.

If that looks right, I’ll lock the Wed slot and we’ll send calendar invites.

Thanks — Neha

Neha — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifying questions from our security team before the deep-dive:

- Where are prompts/request texts stored transiently? Are request/response payloads ever written to disk on Redwood-managed services?

Hi all — following Alice’s questions, here are concrete technical guarantees and configuration choices we can support for a Private/VPC deployment. I’ve tried to separate defaults from configurable options.

Guarantees / configuration options
- Runtime storage: for Private deployments the model servers run inside the customer VPC and use customer-managed EBS volumes. We support two disk modes: encrypted persistent volumes (with BYOK) or ephemeral RAM-only mode. If you select RAM-only, nothing is persisted to disk.
- Request payloads: by default Redwood logs metadata (request id, timestamp, model, route latency) but NOT full payloads in persistent platform logs for Private deployments. If you require, we can set payload_retention = 0 at the platform layer so no request/response payloads are written to any durable storage.
- KV cache: can be configured to be in-memory only and cleared on service restart; for higher throughput options we provide encrypted local cache volumes that are encrypted with the customer KMS and can be wiped on decommission.
- Audit logs: we can emit auth events, admin actions, and request hashes to customer-managed S3 or a syslog endpoint over private connectivity (VPC peering/PrivateLink). Full request bodies are not emitted unless explicitly enabled by mutual agreement.
- Control plane: Redwood Private offers an optional private control plane (customer-managed control plane). If you require fully isolated control plane, we can scope the deployment (additional cost/ops) — otherwise the default control plane will be hosted but will not receive request payloads; only health/metrics telemetry (configurable and can be minimized).
- Network egress: default firewall policy is deny-all egress; we open only customer-approved endpoints (for updates, telemetry endpoints if enabled, object storage endpoints). We can provide exact CIDR/IP ranges and ports for peering.
- BYOK & HSM: support for customer KMS (AWS KMS, CloudHSM) for disk encryption and envelope encryption of any persisted artifacts.
- Air-gapped/on-prem: we ship an offline installer + signed artifact bundle. Key exchange is performed via a secure offline process; we provide an install runbook and a verification checklist.

Artifacts / next items I’ll attach to the invite
- Network IP checklist (required peering ranges + ports)
- Example config to set payload_retention = 0 and KV cache = ram-only
- SOC 2 summary and where to request additional artifacts under NDA

If you want, Marcus and I can run the deep-dive and walk through a demo of the VPC deployment configs. Happy to join Wed.

— Vivek
